learning_outcomes.text: Students know the basic procedure for the design and dimensioning of plastic components and know which mechanical characteristic values are necessary for this and how these characteristic values are determined.

Students can explain how the basic relationships learned in Statics and Strength of Materials for ideal elastic material behavior can be applied to plastic, which exhibits non-linear viscoelastic behavior.

Based on the load cases and environmental conditions, students can decide which material data are required for the design and dimensioning of plastic components and how these data are determined. They select the correct models for stiffness and strength analysis.
Students apply what they have learned in a homework assignment for a practically relevant example. This homework assignment is worked on by a team of several students.

Students apply what they have learned in a homework assignment for a practically relevant example. This homework assignment is worked on by a team of several students. The results are documented in writing.

syllabus_topics: Deepening of materials science for plastics with regard to stress-appropriate design (short-term and long-term behavior static // short-term behavior dynamic (crash) // long-term behavior dynamic (service life))
General introduction to the dimensioning of plastic injection molded components (stiffness and strength analysis)
Dealing with the non-linear viscoelastic behavior of plastics
Execution of stiffness and strength analysis using the example of a "snap hook"
Execution of stiffness and strength analysis using the example of a more complex component from a Finite Element Simulation
Other joining methods such as screwing, welding, gluing
Calculation of a simple practical load case in the homework, e.g., a lid attached to a housing by means of snap hooks.
assessment_rules: The choice of examination type from the given options is at the discretion of the respective examiners. The examination type will be communicated to the students at the beginning of the semester. The homework assignment should be approximately 15-20 pages.
